core_obligations: Settle the top block: since the adjugate satisfies A_1 B = B A_1 = f, the product's first m rows are f times the identity (proof lines 2953-2954).
Compute the lower entries c_ij as the sum over k of a_ik b_kj and rewrite each summand with the signed minor of A_1 (proof lines 2954-2958).
Recognise that expression as the row expansion of the determinant of the matrix displayed in the statement (proof lines 2959-2960).
proof_roadmap: Use the adjugate identity for the square top block (proof lines 2952-2954).
Identify the remaining entries with signed maximal minors by expanding a determinant along a row (proof lines 2954-2961).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the product of an n by m matrix A, with n at least m, by the adjugate of its top m by m block: the top block of the product is the determinant times the identity and the remaining entries are, up to sign, the maximal minors of A obtained by dropping one of the first m rows (statement lines 2922-2950). The proof does not develop a general theory of minors: it invokes the adjugate identity for the top block, writes the lower entries as sums over the index k, and then recognises those sums as row expansions of the relevant determinants (proof lines 2952-2961). The index bookkeeping of that identification is the substance and the author performs it explicitly. H2.
